This real-world testing data will define physics models to represent individual EVSE performance in CHIL devices. Hundreds of these CHIL devices will emulate the charging power of hundreds of EVSE. Although the power transfer from charging will be emulated, each CHIL device will respond to industry standard control signals sent from the SCM. This setup will enable CHIL testing to verify SCM performance at scale and provide a much closer estimate of the actual net power demands of the entire site. This CHIL environment serves as a stress test for the SCM technology and provides results that will closely reflect the control capabilities for transition to field demonstrations and implementation. 3.3.1 EVSE Characterization Characterization of each EVSE listed in Table 1 was performed using the requirements described in Appendix A. The results included in this section are meant to illustrate the type of results that were collected but do not include results for every test. Figure 6 shows results from a 400-VDC nominal power transfer test of the ABB EVSE at ambient temperature (23°C). For this test, the voltage is held constant, while prescribed steps in output current are made that cover as much of the operating area at that voltage level as possible. Use of a vehicle emulator is required for this test, as it requires precise load voltage and current control. The system is allowed to come to steady state for a period of time before the next step is made to gather data at each operating point. This test is then repeated for other voltages within the EVSE’s operating range. This test allows for mapping of metrics like power efficiency over the entire operating range of the EVSE. Figure 6.
